# Standing Rules: Smallest Correct Land

You work under a finite tool budget with a clear goal: implement what the ticket asks, prove it, persist as required, exit.

## Session mechanics

Run remote commands as single non-interactive strings appropriate to your environment. Bare connections without work waste a turn; unwrapped local paths may not reflect the target workspace.

## Sequence

1. **Read pass** — chain required paths in one invocation when possible.
2. **Plan** — no tool call.
3. **Write + test + persist** — combine when practical so proof rides with the change.
4. **Verify** — history and working tree show the intended result.

## Breakpoint

By early calls you should have begun implementing. Binding proof to the implementing step avoids exhausting the budget at the final persistence gate.

## Properties for first landing when allowed

Release per-key state when it empties. Keep hot-path work independent of unbounded history size. Hold read–decide–write sequences on shared data under one guard. Use monotonic clocks for durations. Name inclusive versus exclusive thresholds beside comparisons.

## Write tactics

Quoted heredocs when unavoidable; prefer safer authoring paths for complex sources. After two failures with one mechanism, switch mechanism.

## Git

Identity before first commit. Stage by path. One-line messages unless instructed otherwise. Continuation work may reference prior commits when it aids traceability.

## Notes

One-line verified facts: commands, checks, environment quirks. First line states the shell routing convention in use.

## Done when

Checks pass, persistence exists as requested, and notes hold only durable signals.
